related_questions.question: How long does COVID immunity last after a vaccine?

text_blocks.snippet: The duration of immunity provided by COVID-19 vaccines varies, but generally, protective antibody levels can begin to decline within a few months after vaccination. While mRNA vaccines are effective at preventing severe illness and hospitalization, the antibodies they trigger can fade, potentially leading to breakthrough infections. It's likely that annual COVID-19 vaccine boosters will become the norm to maintain immunity as the virus evolves.

related_questions.question: How long does COVID stay in your system?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 can persist in the body for varying lengths of time, with viral material detectable in some individuals for more than a year after the initial infection. Research indicates that viral components, specifically antigens, can remain in blood and tissue samples for extended periods, potentially contributing to the development of long COVID. While most people recover within a few weeks, some experience ongoing symptoms or conditions that can last for months or even years.
